items.stem: A natural resource that cannot be replaced as fast as people use it is called what?

options.text: A renewable resource
A nonrenewable resource
An endless resource
A living resource

items.explanation: A nonrenewable resource cannot be remade or regrown as fast as we use it, so the supply runs out.

items.stem: Why are fossil fuels considered nonrenewable?

options.text: Living plants make new ones every year
They can be remade in just a few weeks
They take millions of years to form, far longer than we use them
They are made directly out of sunlight

items.explanation: Fossil fuels take hundreds of millions of years to form. We burn them far faster than the Earth can replace them.

items.stem: Which energy resource uses uranium and is nonrenewable because the uranium gets used up?

options.text: Nuclear energy
Solar energy
Wind energy
Geothermal energy

items.explanation: Nuclear energy splits uranium atoms in fission. Uranium is mined and limited, so once it is used it is gone.

items.stem: Which of these is a renewable resource?

options.text: Coal
Natural gas
Petroleum
Wind

items.explanation: Wind is renewable because the Sun keeps heating the air and the wind keeps blowing. The others are fossil fuels.

items.stem: A hydroelectric dam is considered a renewable resource because...

options.text: the water flow is constantly refilled by the water cycle
the concrete dam itself never wears out
it has no effect on the river around it
the water can only be used a single time

items.explanation: Hydroelectric energy uses flowing water, and the water cycle keeps refilling the rivers, so the source returns.

items.stem: As the human population grows, the total demand for natural resources usually...

options.text: stays exactly the same
decreases
disappears
increases

items.explanation: More people need more food, water, energy, and materials, so the total demand for natural resources rises.

options.text: the total number of people on Earth
the amount of resources one person uses
the age of a natural resource
the speed a resource forms underground

items.explanation: Per-capita consumption is the amount of resources a single person uses, which varies with lifestyle and choices.

items.stem: Which change would reduce the energy used for lighting the most?

options.text: leaving the lights on all day
using larger incandescent bulbs
replacing incandescent bulbs with LED bulbs
adding more incandescent bulbs

items.explanation: LED bulbs produce the same light using far less energy, so they cut the resources needed for lighting.

items.stem: Which is the best example of conserving resources?

options.text: recycling materials instead of using new ones
throwing reusable items in the trash
using a new disposable cup every time
leaving the water running while brushing

items.explanation: Recycling reuses materials so fewer new raw materials must be mined or harvested, which conserves resources.

items.stem: A town claims switching to solar and wind power will lower its environmental impact. Which evidence best supports that claim?

options.text: Wind turbines can be very tall
Many towns already have power lines
Solar and wind make electricity without using up fossil fuels
Solar panels are usually a dark color

items.explanation: Evidence must connect to the claim. Solar and wind generate electricity without burning nonrenewable fossil fuels, which lowers impact.
